newsitem.title: HUNGARY: IEB TO PAY 12.5PCT DIVIDEND, RAISE CAPITAL.
newsitem.headline: IEB TO PAY 12.5PCT DIVIDEND, RAISE CAPITAL.

text.p: BUDAPEST, April 25 - Hungary's Inter-Europa Bank pays 12.5 percent dividend on the 1996 earnings and will raise its capital in 1997 to at least seven billion forints from 2.8 billion, Inter-Europa's shareholders decided on Thursday.
The bank, in which the biggest single shareholder, San Paolo Bank of Italy has special managerial positions, paid 12.5 dividend plus 2.5 dividend premium on the 1995 earnings.
The bank's annual shareholders meeting decided to double the bank's registered capital from the profit reserves of 3.65 billion forints.

The capital increase gives Inter-Europa shareholders a bonus share on each share they will have on a day, to be defined later by the board of directors following the capital hike's court registration which is expected for August.

The shares from the capital increase will be floated on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) and this is likely to push down the price of Inter-Europa shares there, said Pier Franco Rubatto, Chief Executive Officer of the bank.

Matematically, the flotation should halve the price on the BSE, but Inter-Europa officials said they hoped the price would remain higher than that and was expected to rise as the capital increase would improve the bank's outlook.
"The advantage of the bank will be that the registered capital doubles and this promotes the bank's image," Chairman Laszlo Body said.

According to Hungarian regulations, the current registered capital allows Inter-Europa to lend maximum 1.8 billion forints to one single client, while some creditworthy customers needed more, Rubatto added.

The meeting also decided that after the first capital increase the bank will publicly offer new shares worth 1.4 billion forints. Inter-Europa shareholders will have a pre-emption right to buy one new share upon each four shares they have.

To the proposal of a small shareholder, the board of directors will decide whether an extraordinary shareholders' meeting after the first capital increase should be summoned to raise the limit of the second capital hike.
Inter-Europa's balance sheet total rose to 90.8 billion forints last year from 62.4 billion in 1995, while average inflation was 23.6 billion forints in 1996.
The bank boosted its net income to 1.28 billion forints in 1996 from 816 million in 1995.
Inter-Europa expects its pre-tax profit, which rose to 2.086 billion forints last year from 1.78 billion in 1995, to increase to 2.5 billion forints this year, Rubatto said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Inter-Europa Bank shares closed at 50,000 forints, up 200 forints.
